fullPassage: The International Space Station, or ISS, is the ninth space station to be inhabited by humans. Since 2000, it has been continuously occupied by astronauts. It serves as a research laboratory for many fields, including astronomy, physics, and medicine. It is also used to test spacecraft systems required for possible future missions to the moon, Mars, and asteroids. As big as a football field, it is composed of many different sections, such as experiment modules, habitation modules, solar battery panels, and robotic arms. It is a completely unique structure assembled by spacewalkers flying around Earth at 28,000 kilometers per hour in a vacuum in extremes of temperature of plus and minus 270 degrees Celsius. It is the result of work by 15 different nations over about two decades. The work was carried out by thousands of people speaking different languages and using different engineering methods and standards. Putting the space station into orbit, making it work, and keeping it working are perhaps some of the most difficult things that human beings have ever done. In January 2022, NASA announced a plan to de-orbit the ISS in 2030. Many astronauts believe that it will stand forever as proof that when humans work together, we can do anything from going to Mars to solving our problems here on Earth.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: habitation(거주): inhabit에서 접두사 in- 제거 후 명사형 -ation.
det.analysis: inhabit(동사, 거주하다) → habitation(명사, 거주). 'habitation modules'는 복합명사로, 명사+명사 구조. experiment modules와 병렬.
det.tip: inhabit → habitation. 접두사 in-을 떼고 -ation 접미사 결합.

questions.passage: It is a completely unique structure assembled by spacewalkers flying around Earth at 28,000 kilometers per hour in a vacuum in extremes of temperature of plus and minus 270 degrees Celsius. It is the result of work by 15 different nations over about two decades. The work was __________ by thousands of people speaking different languages and using different engineering methods and standards. Putting the space station into orbit, making it work, and keeping it working are perhaps some of the most difficult things that human beings have ever done.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 수행되었다(carried out): 수천 명이 작업을 수행했다.
det.analysis:
① given up(포기한): 포기가 아니라 완수한 작업
② turned down(거절한): 작업을 거절한 것이 아님
③ carried out(수행한): 수천 명이 다양한 언어와 공학 기준으로 작업 수행 ← 정답
④ held back(억제한): 작업을 억제한 것이 아님
det.tip: carry out = 수행하다. The work was carried out = 작업이 수행되었다.

questions.passage: The International Space Station, or ISS, is the ninth space station to be inhabited by humans. Since 2000, it has been continuously occupied by astronauts. It serves as a research laboratory for many fields, including astronomy, physics, and medicine. It is also used to test spacecraft systems required for possible future missions to the moon, Mars, and asteroids. As big as a football field, it is __________ many different sections, such as experiment modules, habitation modules, solar battery panels, and robotic arms.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ~로 구성되어 있다(composed of): 다양한 섹션들로 이루어진 구조물.
det.analysis:
① deprived of(~을 빼앗긴): 구성 요소를 나열하는 문맥과 반대
② composed of(~로 구성된): 실험 모듈, 거주 모듈 등으로 구성 — 원문 일치 ← 정답
③ superior to(~보다 우수한): 비교 대상이 없으므로 부적절
④ familiar with(~에 익숙한): ISS가 섹션에 익숙하다는 표현 부자연스러움
det.tip: be composed of = be made up of = consist of. ~로 구성되다.
